text: Federated classifiers can appear reliable on average yet become unsafe when future traffic shifts toward a difficult client. This study asks which predictions from a fixed federated open-set classifier may be automated when the client mixture is uncertain. Client-dependent acceptance changes the mixture among automated predictions, so the relevant selective risk is a ratio whose numerator and denominator both depend on traffic. FedCORE represents traffic uncertainty by a credal set and sampling uncertainty by finite-sample client audits. Using audit size, accepted count, and accepted-error count, it returns a deploy-or-refuse decision without retraining. We establish a fixed-pooling reducibility boundary, an exact full-simplex certificate, a positive-denominator program for strict credal polytopes, and familywise-valid selection among proposal-frozen rules. In target-matched replay over 443 proposal-feasible empirical-reservoir conditions, the minimum observed coverage was 0.953 and none fell below 0.95. With the full-simplex target, predictors, selector families, budgets, and counts held fixed, the Holm intersection-union procedure certified 177 of 450 conditions with mean effective certified acceptance of 8.34%, whereas valid fixed-prior betting certified 81 with 3.97%. In Office-Home, changing the protected target from the full simplex to an independently formed traffic-informed credal set increased certifications from 74 to 92 of 100 and mean effective certified acceptance from 9.6% to 19.3%. This was target sensitivity, not a same-target method comparison. A 30-model PACS rerun and pre-specified VLCS and DomainNet fixed-frame evaluations failed primary utility or transfer gates. The results distinguish validity of a credal deployment decision from utility of the predictor and evidence budget.
